author: Astra
target: J293/T8103 Broadcom BCM4378 on APCIE port0

answers.PERST_GPIO: CONFIRMED: main AP GPIO pin152. This is decoded from the actual saved J293 bridge0 function-perst property and its unique phandle provider in two independently retained ADT blobs; it is not inherited merely from the older candidate note.
answers.own_power_rail: A separate Wi-Fi/Bluetooth module-enable path is supported by pinned m1n1: SMC GPIO13, keygP0d. It is shared radio power/enable, not an independently established Wi-Fi-only rail. The ADT does not declare its relationship as a bridge/wlan power-enable property; no electrical rail schematic or current level is established. PERST or APCIE controller power alone is not proof that the radio is enabled. Conversely, this source evidence does not prove a new toggle is necessary if the enable is already asserted at handoff.

PERST_interpretation.raw_cell_format: m1n1 adt.py Function interprets phandle as LE32, function name through FourCC, then LE32 argument words. utils.py FourCC renders the integer in big-endian character order. 0x4750494f therefore denotes GPIO.
PERST_interpretation.decoded: phandle119 resolves to /arm-io/gpio, function GPIO, arguments152 and0. The main AP GPIO compatible isgpio,t8101 and has212pins, so152 is in range.
PERST_interpretation.independent_of_CLKREQ: The adjacent function-clkreq uses the same provider but arguments150 and2; pin150 is not PERST.
PERST_interpretation.internal_port_reset_is_separate: Pinned src/pcie.c defines the internal APCIE port-reset register at0x814 and reset-disable bit0. The T8103 path sets that bit before polling RUN. It does not execute the ADT function-perst GPIO callback. The internal register and external AP GPIO152 must not be conflated.
PERST_interpretation.polarity_scope: PERST# is the external reset signal name; the final ADT argument0 is preserved as an opaque function argument here, not reinterpreted as Linux GPIO flags or an instruction to write a GPIO level. No pin direction/mux/lock/level was read on hardware.
PERST_interpretation.delay_metadata: Both retained bridge nodes have t-refclk-to-perst=100 and perst-to-config=100. The ADT alone does not label units in these raw values; no timing recipe is invented from them.

radio_enable_evidence.finding: The MIT experiment names pin13 in its Wi-Fi/Bluetooth enable example and forms SMC GPIO keys from the pin number. Its example would selectgP0d and use the0x800000 control bit with a low/high value. Those example lines are commented source, not a recorded run or board-specific electrical specification.

A separate MIT PCIe-device enable experiment starts the SMC client/endpoint0x20 and writesgP0d with0x800001. This corroborates an SMC-controlled endpoint-enable dependency beyond PCIe core initialization. The script is an unrestricted experiment, imports m1n1.setup and is not safe to execute as a discovery operation.
The same experiment also writesgP1a. It does not name that key’s device or document a J293 requirement. Do not copy that extra write into a Wi-Fi bring-up sequence or claim it belongs to BCM4378.

A separate SMC GPIO provider exists with16pins, supporting the existence of a different GPIO controller from main AP GPIO. Pin13 is in that provider range. The tree does not expose an explicit wlan-to-pin13 power-enable edge, so range membership alone is not wiring proof.

pcie_init enables APCIE PMGR/controller/PHY/port state but contains no endpoint SMC GPIO operation and no function-perst/function-clkreq execution. A successful PCIe initializer return would not certify external PERST152 or SMC radio-enable state.

older_Linux_DT_claim.previous_claim: An older report named port00 pwren-gpios referencing smc_gpio13.
older_Linux_DT_claim.source_status: The earlier ownership report labeled that an unpinned local secondary cross-check. No t8103/J293 DTS file was found in the current local source workspace for re-verification in this task. No fetch was performed.
older_Linux_DT_claim.use_in_this_conclusion: Not treated as independently verified primary DT evidence. The new primary conclusions use actual saved J293 ADT bytes and exact pinned MIT m1n1 source.

recommended_contract_for_later_driver: Resolve PERST through the actual bridge function’s provider and pin every boot; never hardcode Linux/ADT phandle numbers interchangeably.
Treat main AP GPIO152, internal port-reset-disable, and shared SMC radio-enable13 as three distinct resources with distinct owners. Preserve sibling Bluetooth state.

Before a later owned reset/link transaction, establish whether the SMC radio-enable is already on or acquire a genuine reviewed SMC control service. Missing ownership/state is NOT_READY, not permission to toggle.
Do not invoke the general m1n1 pcie_enable_devices experiment, copygP1a, reset a shared rail, or assume a successful PMGR/PHY sequence powers the BCM4378.
This note proposes no writes or host/source changes. Any later power/reset transaction needs separate bounded implementation/source/packet review and the unchanged Linux-recovery contract.
method: Read local source as data, verify against exact local Git objects, and parse only saved ADT blobs with the existing pure parser function extracted as AST. No m1n1 runtime/transport module imported or experiment executed.
